chunks: And Ali ibn Ahmad informed us, from Ubaydillah ibn Musa, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abban ibn Uthman, from al-Fadl ibn Yasar, who said:

I heard Abu Abdullah Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) saying: 'Whoever invites people to follow him while there is among them someone better than him, he is a deviate and a heretic. And whoever claims Imamate from Allah while he is not an Imam, he is an unbeliever.'
ai.seo_question: What distinguishes a true Imam from a pretender in Shia theology?
ai.summary: In the context of the era of the Minor and Major Occultation, this hadith from al-Nu'mani’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* serves as a critical tool for distinguishing authentic Imams from pretenders (*da'awat al-khawa*). It establishes two distinct criteria: the error of self-promotion when a superior authority is present, and the grave sin of false divine claim, reinforcing the Shia doctrine of *Nass* (divine designation) over mere merit or popular acclaim.
